details.label: Summary
details.text: A few instances of large hail and damaging wind will be possible this afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorm activity has increased in coverage along the high terrain across eastern New Mexico and eastern Colorado this afternoon. This activity will slowly spread into the lower plains through the afternoon and evening. Deep layer shear for organization is best across eastern Colorado, with weaker shear across eastern New Mexico. The most favorable instability also resides across eastern Colorado. A few isolated supercells with large hail will be possible initially. Large dew point depressions and steep low level lapse rates will likely lead to outflow dominate storms and more of a threat for strong to severe wind. Overall, this threat should remain too localized for watch issuance

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated severe storms may develop along a west-to-east oriented boundary through the remainder of the afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Scattered thunderstorms have been increasing in intensity along a diffuse west-to-east oriented boundary extending from central and northern Illinois into western Ohio. Along this boundary, over 1000 J/kg MLCAPE is in place, along with substantial 0-3 km CAPE (150-175 J/kg). Furthermore, an 80 kt 300 mb jet streak is overspreading the OH Valley, contributing to 50+ kts of effective bulk shear (mainly speed shear in the mid to upper levels per RAP forecast soundings). Given these conditions, the current thinking is that a few of the stronger storms along this baroclinic boundary may become transient supercellular, capable of producing a couple instances of severe wind/hail or even a brief tornado

details.text: An isolated supercell appears possible based on recent satellite trends. Isolated large hail and severe winds are possible should a storm develop. A watch is not likely

details.label: Discussion
details.text: An area of agitated cumulus has developed in northwest Kansas over the last hour along a weak surface cold front. Very weak ascent aloft from a glancing shortwave trough in the central Plains could allow an isolated supercell to develop. Visible satellite trends and some recent CAM guidance would suggest storm initiation is probable, though not certain. The environment would support isolated large hail and severe winds. Given the lack of greater upper-level support, coverage and duration of severe intensity will likely be limited

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorm activity will continue to slowly increase and spread westward off the higher terrain through 2-4 PM MST. A severe weather watch may be needed at some point, once storms begin to consolidate into an evolving cluster, but this may not be until later this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Substantive destabilization is ongoing across much of central and southern Arizona, within a seasonably moist air mass boosted by a recent surge from the Gulf of California. Latest objective analysis indicates that strongest potential instability has become focused to immediate southwest and west of the higher terrain of east central into southeastern Arizona, where inhibition has been eroding most appreciably. As this continues over the next few hours, a slow propagation off the higher terrain straddling the southern Arizona/New Mexico border may commence by 21-23Z, with strong downbursts posing increasing potential for strong to severe surface gusts within a strongly heated and deep mixed boundary-layer. Increasing thunderstorm development closer to the southeastern Arizona international border may also begin to impact the Tucson vicinity
